newsitem.title: UK: Treasuries sidelined in London as payrolls loom.
newsitem.headline: Treasuries sidelined in London as payrolls loom.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries were little moved in London as the prospect of key employment data out of the U.S. later on kept many investors on the sidelines, traders said.
"People are quite neutral going into this number," said a trader at a U.S. house. "There is money to be spent, and there could be a good rise on the back of a number like 100,000."
The consensus forecast according to a Reuters poll is for a rise of 237,000 in January, compared with 262,000 previously. The data were scheduled to be released at 1330 GMT.
U.S. 30-year long bond was at 96-20, yielding 6.75 percent versus 96-22 in Tokyo and 96-22 at the New York close.
March T-bond futures were down 2/32 at 111-27 in automated trade by 0955 GMT.

Average hourly earnings data will be closely watched for signs of inflationary pressures building into the economy. The forecast was for a rise of 0.2 percent. The unemployment rate is expected to stand at 5.2 percent, down from 5.3 percent.

Analysts at Bank of America said a rise in earnings of more than 0.2 percent would be bad news for the asset markets, and if combined with a high payroll number could even trigger a rise in interest rates before the next Federal Open Market Committee meeting in March.
